reader_standard: minimum open space for townhouse-style development
reader_about: design standards for Gresham's Civic Neighborhood Plan District covering solid waste screening, streetscape glazing, tree/landscaping, fencing, lighting, entries, parapets, and signage for multiple building types, including standards explicitly labeled "Townhouse Style" and "Multi-Family and Townhouse"
reader_note: "S10. Open Space for Townhouse Style. A minimum of 15 percent of the gross lot area of the development shall be included as outdoor open space" (L2289) applies directly to a four-unit attached townhouse building; L2310 caps hardscape at 50 percent of that space and L2820's Multi-Family/Townhouse fencing standard (max 4 ft in a required front setback) also applies. This is a mapped Plan District overlay, but a lot inside it must still meet these standards.

reader_standard: minimum open space for townhouse-style development
reader_about: design standards for Gresham's Rockwood Design District, structured almost identically to the Civic Neighborhood Plan District, covering screening, glazing, landscaping, fencing, lighting, entries, and signage, including standards explicitly for "Townhouse Style" and "Multi-Family and Townhouse" development
reader_note: "S10. Open Space for Townhouse Style. A minimum of 15 percent of the gross lot area of the development shall be included as outdoor open space" (L1661) applies directly to our four-unit attached townhouse; L1682 caps hardscape at 50 percent and L2126's Multi-Family/Townhouse fencing standard (max 4 ft in front yard setback) also applies. This is a mapped design district, but a lot inside it must still comply.

reader_standard: minimum open space for townhouse-style development
reader_about: design standards for Gresham's Downtown Plan Design District covering front-setback consistency, screening, glazing, landscaping, fencing, entries, parapets, and signage, including a "Townhouse Style" open-space standard and "Multi-Family and Townhouse" fencing
reader_note: "S8. Open Space for Townhouse Style. A minimum of 15 percent of the gross lot area of the development shall be included as outdoor open space" (L2424) applies directly to a four-unit townhouse building; L2445 caps hardscape at 50 percent, and L1557's front-setback-consistency rule (a multi-family setback must be within 5 ft of an abutting single-detached dwelling's setback, capped at 15 ft) could also bind depending on the abutting lot.

reader_about: detailed development standards for Milwaukie's Downtown Mixed Use (DMU) zone: minimum building height along street frontage, optional height bonuses, and minimum residential density for townhouses and stand-alone multifamily
reader_note: "Minimum densities for townhouses and live/work units are 25 units per acre" (L2026) effectively caps the buildable lot size for a fixed four-unit townhouse building at roughly 0.16 acres in this zone. L1882's "minimum building height of 25 ft ... along all street frontages" also applies to any building here, though our ~26 ft design already clears it; L1894/L1902/L1908/L1914 are elective height bonuses, not requirements.

reader_about: design standards (perimeter fencing, walkways, driveway width, tree planting, building height, common green, fenced dog area) specific to Cottage Cluster housing developments in Gresham
reader_note: The section heading "7.0440 COTTAGE CLUSTER DESIGN STANDARDS" scopes every marked line to Cottage Cluster developments; our building is explicitly not a cottage cluster.

reader_about: height and footprint standards for detached accessory structures (garages, sheds), plus fence height limits by zone and a stand-alone flagpole height limit, in Milwaukie
reader_note: The section is "§ 19.502.2. Specific Provisions for Accessory Structures," and the marked lines govern accessory-structure roof pitch (L259/L273), fences (L309/L327/L333), and flagpoles (L345) — accessory structures and fences are both explicitly excluded categories, not the primary dwelling.

reader_about: downtown design elements for Milwaukie: ground-floor height, corner/facade articulation features (tower/turret, corner offset, vertical offset, dormer), and an elevator/mechanical-equipment height-exceedance allowance
reader_note: L3099's ground-floor-height standard doesn't state whether it excludes residential use, and this same document's parallel design-standard sections elsewhere in the corpus scope ground-floor-height rules to commercial/institutional space specifically — the excerpt shown doesn't say which applies here. The corner-articulation lines (L3757/L3761/L3851/L3855) read as items in an options menu whose required count isn't shown in this excerpt. The page genuinely doesn't let us tell whether any of this binds a residential-only building.

reader_about: permitted reductions to yard setbacks within specific Planned Development Residential zones (PDR-7-S, PDR-4-S, PDR-1-S) in Wilsonville, alongside an unrelated solar-access shade-height table
reader_note: "A front yard setback may be reduced to not less than ..." (L11089 and similar) states a floor on an optional, discretionary setback reduction within specific PDR zones — an allowance a developer may choose to use, not a standard the building must meet.

reader_about: design standards (perimeter screening/fence height, interior open space) specific to Manufactured Dwelling Park developments in Gresham
reader_note: The section heading "7.0410 MANUFACTURED DWELLING PARK DESIGN STANDARDS" scopes every marked line to manufactured dwelling parks, a building type explicitly excluded from our brief.

reader_standard: minimum on-site tree area for one-to-four-family residential development
reader_about: Portland's on-site tree density/tree-area standard, giving a required percentage of site area (or an area-minus-building-coverage alternative) that must be planted with trees, broken out by development type
reader_note: The table's "One to Four Family Residential" row (L170) requires "40 percent of site or development impact area" under Option A, or "Site area minus building coverage of existing and proposed development" under Option B — our four-unit attached building falls squarely in this development-type row.

reader_about: definitions and siting standards for wireless communication facilities and antenna support structures (towers, small wireless facilities) in Happy Valley
reader_note: Every marked line concerns antenna/wireless-facility height (existing structures used as antenna supports, tower modifications) — a different use entirely from our residential building, which includes no telecom infrastructure.

reader_about: a step-back requirement for buildings exceeding the base maximum height in Milwaukie's General Mixed Use (GMU) zone, plus optional height bonuses for residential use, green-building certification, and other incentives
reader_note: L1132's step-back only applies to "any street-facing portion of the building above the base maximum height" — a mixed-use zone's base height ceiling is well above our fixed ~26 ft, two-story design — and L1148/L1154/L1160 are elective incentive bonuses ("permitted," not required).

reader_about: development standards (home size, height, setbacks, garage door width) specific to Cottage Cluster housing in Milwaukie
reader_note: Table 19.505.4.C.1 is titled "Cottage Cluster Development Standards" and section 19.505.4 is "Cottage Cluster Housing" — our building is explicitly not a cottage cluster.

reader_about: an optional corner architectural treatment feature and conditional height allowances for roof-mounted equipment (small equipment exemption, elevator equipment, satellite dishes/mechanical equipment) in Milwaukie
reader_note: L2667/L2671/L2675 are allowances letting rooftop equipment exceed the height limit only if such equipment is installed ("may extend," limits on equipment that may or may not exist), mirroring the height-exception pattern seen elsewhere in this batch; L2474 offers a corner treatment "such as" one example among options, not a stated requirement on the building itself.

reader_about: fence height standards by yard location for single-dwelling zones in unincorporated Multnomah County, alongside an unrelated table of institutional-development site standards (building coverage, landscaping, buffering)
reader_note: The section is titled "Fences," an explicitly excluded category; Table 110-9's content in the same passage is scoped to "Institutional Development," a use our building is not.

reader_about: height-limit exceptions allowing rooftop projections — chimneys, flagpoles, satellite dishes, parapets, elevator/mechanical equipment — to exceed the district height limit, in unincorporated Multnomah County
reader_note: Every marked line is a permissive allowance ("may rise," "may extend") for optional rooftop features exceeding the base height limit, not a standard our building must meet — matches the brief's "permitted projection ... nothing has to be satisfied" case.

reader_about: standards for detached accessory dwellings (cottages) and other accessory structures — height and setback limits based on distance from the property line — in Fairview
reader_note: L829 governs "detached accessory dwellings," and L885/L891/L893 govern "accessory structures" — both explicitly excluded categories from our brief; none of the marked lines address the primary dwelling.

reader_about: height limits for optional roof-mounted and ground-mounted solar and wind energy systems, plus general building and outdoor-facility setbacks, in Gresham's Pleasant Valley plan districts
reader_note: The marked lines all fall under "RENEWABLE ENERGY STANDARDS ... Solar energy systems are limited ... as follows," governing voluntarily-installed accessory equipment, not a standard the building itself must meet.

reader_about: height-limit exceptions allowing rooftop projections — chimneys, flagpoles, satellite dishes, parapets, elevator/mechanical equipment — to exceed the district height limit, in Portland (identical text to unincorporated Multnomah's 33.140.210)
reader_note: Every marked line is a permissive allowance ("may rise," "may extend") for optional rooftop features, not a standard our building must meet.

reader_about: a lot-coverage bonus (+10 or +5 percentage points) for single detached dwellings, most middle housing types, and accessory dwelling units, for portions of structures 20 ft tall or less, in Milwaukie
reader_note: L309 explicitly carves out "except for townhouses and cottage clusters" from the middle-housing lot-coverage bonus — our four-unit, townhouse-style building is expressly excluded; L305 and L320 apply to single-detached dwellings and ADUs, different building types, and all three are elective bonuses rather than requirements.

reader_about: fence, hedge, wall, and retaining wall height standards by location, in Oregon City
reader_note: The section is titled "Fences, hedges, walls, and retaining walls" — an explicitly excluded category; none of the marked lines govern the dwelling itself.

reader_about: a height exception for buildings on steep lots (grade differential greater than 10 ft) in West Linn, allowing greater total building height when measured from the downhill grade point
reader_note: This is a permissive exception ("may exceed the building height standard, provided ...") available to buildings wanting to build taller than the base limit on a steep lot; our fixed ~26 ft, two-story building doesn't need or trigger it.

reader_about: street tree species and minimum planting-height standards (evergreen trees at least 12 ft, species lists by mature height) for public street-frontage plantings, in Wilsonville
reader_note: This falls under "D. Street Trees," governing plantings in the public right-of-way frontage improvement ("the Development Review Board may require a mix of street trees throughout a development") — a public improvement, not a standard on the building itself.

reader_standard: minimum ground floor height for residential use
reader_about: base design requirements for Fairview's storefront/design-standard districts, giving required and optional (point-scored) ground-floor height, glazing, and landscaping standards
reader_note: "For ground floor area associated with a residential use, the height is 10 feet" (L408), listed as "Required" (R1) in Table 19.65.090(B)(1) for both the Storefront District and elsewhere — this directly applies to our residential ground floor. L617 and L620 are optional point-menu items ("may be landscaped," an "Additional" height option worth points), not required.

reader_about: lot coverage and building height standards for uses along the Columbia River north of Marine Drive in the General Industrial District
reader_note: "The maximum allowable lot coverage in the general industrial district is 90 percent" and the 60/70-foot height standards govern the General Industrial District; a residential-only fourplex is not a use this section's district accommodates.

reader_about: an affordable-housing density and height bonus table
reader_note: Table 10.1711(B) grants extra 'DENSITY BONUS' and 'HEIGHT BONUS' only to a project that provides affordable units. It is an optional bonus a developer may choose to pursue, not a number the building must satisfy.

reader_about: definitions of tree-related terms (clear cutting, crown cover, diameter breast height) used elsewhere in the tree code
reader_note: "The following definitions apply to Tree-related applications" — this is a definitions section stating what terms mean, not an operative standard the building must meet.

reader_about: height limits for optional roof-mounted and ground-mounted solar energy systems in residential districts
reader_note: "Ground-mounted. Systems shall not exceed 6 feet in height" and the roof-mounted limits apply only if a solar energy system is installed. The fourplex is not required to have one, so nothing here must be satisfied.

reader_about: height limits for optional roof-mounted and ground-mounted solar energy systems in the Springwater plan district
reader_note: "Ground-mounted solar energy systems shall not exceed 20 feet in height" only applies if the building owner chooses to install a solar system; it is not a standard the fourplex itself must meet.

reader_about: fence height limits within required setbacks in single-dwelling zones
reader_note: "Fences up to 8 feet high are allowed in required side or rear building setbacks" governs an accessory fence, which the instructions treat as its own excluded category — it says nothing about the dwelling itself.

reader_about: definitions of ceiling-height exclusions and 'Living Area' used to calculate floor area
reader_note: "Living Area. The total gross building area of a residential structure excluding the following..." is a definitions section, not an operative standard.

reader_about: minimum and step-down maximum building heights for new buildings on Halsey Street, including transitions near residential zones
reader_note: "There is a minimum height of eighteen (18) feet or one and one-half (1.5) stories for all new buildings on Halsey Street" applies to all new buildings with no stated use exception, so a new fourplex here would have to meet it (our 26-foot, two-storey design clears it easily). The step-down maximums at L66/L72 (35-45 ft) only bind if the lot is near a residential zone, which the passage doesn't establish here.

reader_about: setback standards for cottage cluster development
reader_note: "Cottage clusters shall meet the minimum setback standards" — the section heading and text are scoped explicitly to cottage clusters, a housing type distinct from a four-unit attached building on one lot.

reader_about: setback standards for cottage cluster development
reader_note: "Cottage clusters shall meet the minimum setback standards" — same cottage-cluster-only scoping as 17.10.055; not our building type.

reader_about: design standards for the ground floor of buildings in the MUTSA and on NME Key Streets, including a street-wall-area definition and a minimum ground-floor height
reader_note: "The ground-floor height must be at least 14 ft, as measured from the finished floor to the ceiling..." is stated for 'All Uses' in the MUTSA / NME Key Streets area; a fourplex built on a lot inside that mapped area would have to meet it. L4157's 15-foot street-wall-area definition is a related measurement rule for the same mapped standards.

reader_about: dimensional standards table for the R-2 zone, which lists quadplex as a permitted use with its own minimum lot size, alongside general setback and coverage standards
reader_note: "Minimum rear yard setback 10 feet" is listed under 'All, except' with quadplex not named as an exception, so it applies to our building. L4598's 'Maximum front yard setback 20 feet' is the same kind of general standard and also binds.

reader_about: minimum size, width, coverage, and spacing standards for creating a 'small lot' within a subdivision
reader_note: "(2) Minimum Lot Size and Location. The small lot must:..." reads as a land-division standard for a specific small-lot configuration (with cul-de-sac frontage tests), not a general zone development standard shown to cover a four-unit attached building.

reader_about: minimum lot size and setback standards for the FDA-H Future Development Agricultural-Holding Zone
reader_note: The zone name itself — 'Future Development Agricultural—Holding Zone' — signals a holding designation pending future planning; nothing here suggests a four-unit residential building is a use this district accommodates.

reader_about: exceptions to the maximum height and alternative height limits for steeply sloping lots, within the Institutional Development Standards
reader_note: Both marked lines sit inside 33.110.270, 'Institutional Development Standards,' which governs institutional uses (schools, churches, and similar), not a residential building.

reader_about: site area, FAR, height and setback standards for institutional uses in Table 110-9
reader_note: Table 110-9, 'Institutional Development Standards,' governs institutional uses; a residential fourplex is a different use category entirely.

reader_about: sign dimension standards (area, height, width, base) for Fairview Village
reader_note: "Maximum face area of 75 square feet" and "Height shall be a maximum of 12 feet" govern a sign structure, an excluded category, not the dwelling.

reader_about: fence height limits for recreational courts, swimming pools, and electric fences
reader_note: "A wire fence not to exceed 12 feet in height" and the swimming-pool/electric-fence limits are accessory fence standards, not a standard the building itself must satisfy.

reader_about: rear and side setback standards in the Light Industrial District
reader_note: "There is no required rear setback, except that buildings shall be setback from the residential district by a minimum of 20 feet" governs the Light Industrial District's use table (industrial/commercial uses), where a residential-only fourplex is not listed as a use.

reader_about: purpose/intent statement for the MDR-12 district describing maximum net densities for single detached dwellings, manufactured dwelling parks, and townhouses
reader_note: "...single detached dwellings of 12.1 units per acre, manufactured dwelling parks at a maximum net density of 8.71 units per acre, and townhouses at a maximum net density of 25 units per acre" names three specific housing types; a four-unit building on one lot is a quadplex/multifamily building, a different category than any of the three named here.

reader_about: height limits for optional roof-mounted wind energy systems in residential districts
reader_note: "Wind energy systems shall not exceed the district height limit... and shall not exceed 10 feet above the height of the roof" applies only if a wind energy system is installed; it is not required equipment.

reader_about: height limits for optional solar energy systems in Commercial Districts, in a section adjoining (but distinct from) commercial building-height and outdoor-activity standards
reader_note: The marked lines — "frames shall not exceed 10 feet above the roof height" and "Ground-mounted solar energy systems shall not exceed 20 feet in height" — are optional solar-equipment standards scoped to section 4.0232, Solar Energy Standards for Commercial Districts; nothing marked here is a standard the residential fourplex itself must meet.

reader_about: height limits for optional solar energy systems in Corridor Districts
reader_note: "Ground-mounted solar energy systems shall not exceed 20 feet in height" applies only if a solar system is installed; it is optional equipment, not a required building standard.

reader_about: height limits for optional roof-mounted and ground-mounted wind energy systems in the Springwater plan district
reader_note: "Ground-mounted wind energy systems shall not exceed 110 feet in height" applies only if a wind energy system is installed; it is optional equipment, not a required building standard.

reader_about: institutional development standards for schools, religious institutions, hospitals and similar institutional uses -- height exceptions and alternative height limits for steeply sloping lots
reader_note: The headings state "33.110.270, Institutional Development Standards" and Table 110-4 is 'for institutional uses'; both marked lines (L554 rooftop-equipment height exception, L595 sloped-lot height alternative) are exceptions inside that institutional standards chapter, which does not govern a residential fourplex.

reader_about: institutional development standards table (minimum site area, FAR, height, setbacks) for institutional uses
reader_note: Passage is Table 110-9, "Institutional Development Standards[1]", with L1978 maximum height (50 ft) and L1979 minimum building setbacks stated for institutional development -- a different use than our residential building.

reader_about: minimum width of the on-site pedestrian circulation system, scaled to the number of dwelling units it serves
reader_note: L1654: "Segments of the circulation system that connect only to an entrance providing access to up to 4 units may be 3 feet wide" -- exactly our 4-unit building. The unmarked L1647-48 sets the same 3-foot minimum for "sites with up to 4 residential units."

reader_about: reduced side setbacks for detached houses created by a land division, and a height limit tied to a detached accessory structure
reader_note: L1718's reduced setback applies only to "detached houses" from a land division, and L1762's 25-foot height limit sits in the same subsection as a "detached accessory structure" (L1760-61); neither applies to an attached four-unit building.

reader_about: optional floor-area-ratio and height bonuses (inclusionary housing, affordable commercial space, planned development) above the base zone maximums
reader_note: Table 130-3 is "Summary of Bonus FAR and Height" -- every marked row (L731, L733) is an elective increment "per bonus" a developer may choose to pursue; nothing here must be satisfied.

reader_about: minimum size of trees and shrubs planted as required landscaping, including hedges used to screen and buffer off-street parking from adjoining properties
reader_note: L326: "Trees shall be a minimum of seven (7) feet in overall height or one and one half (1 1/2) inches in caliper immediately after planting." Our building has off-street parking that L336 ties a screening/buffering hedge requirement to, so these planting-size minimums would apply to the lot's required landscaping.

reader_about: manufactured home park minimum street frontage, park depth, and perimeter screening standards
reader_note: Section 8.160 is titled "Manufactured Home Parks," a use type our four-unit attached building is not.

reader_about: optional density bonus for affordable housing and mixed-use development, plus the footnote formula for computing the "base density" used in that bonus calculation
reader_note: Table 1012-1 is "Bonus Density," an elective increase; L210 is footnote 2 explaining how base density is computed (gross site area / 43,560 sq ft per unit) solely to size the bonus, not a standard applied directly to our building.

reader_about: residential design standards in the R-7.2 zone: recessed garage entrance, roof pitch, and garage/carport requirement
reader_note: L293: "Roof pitch of not less than three feet in height for each 12 feet in width" (a 3:12 minimum pitch). The section is titled plainly "Design standards" (unlike the next section, which is explicitly limited to cottage clusters), reading as the zone's general residential design standard, which would include a middle-housing fourplex.

reader_about: cottage cluster design standards (detached garage floor area and garage door width limits)
reader_note: Section title is "17.10.065 Cottage cluster design standards" -- our building is a four-unit attached townhome, not a cottage cluster.

reader_about: residential design standards in the R-5 zone: recessed garage entrance, roof pitch, and garage/carport requirement
reader_note: Same pattern as the R-7.2 zone's 17.10.060: L298 sets a minimum 3-foot-rise-per-12-foot roof pitch under a generically titled "Design standards" section, distinct from the cottage-cluster-only section immediately after it.

reader_about: cottage cluster design standards (detached garage floor area and garage door width limits)
reader_note: Section title is "17.12.065 Cottage cluster design standards" -- not our building type.

reader_about: definition of how existing tree diameter (DBH) is measured for tree-preservation purposes
reader_note: This is a measurement-methodology definition ("Existing trees are measured at a height 4.5 ft above the mean ground level..."), not a standard our building must satisfy.

reader_about: dimensional development standards (lot size, frontage, FAR, front setback) for the North Milwaukie Innovation Area base zone's MUTSA and NME subareas
reader_note: L3976 sets a maximum front yard setback (10 ft in MUTSA, 30 ft on NME key streets), but the passage never states whether a stand-alone residential fourplex is even a permitted use in this "Innovation Area" zone -- the visible table gives only dimensional standards, not a use list, so applicability can't be told from this page.

reader_about: exemption from process review for trimming plants/vegetation adjacent to trails
reader_note: L717 sets a trim-clearance limit (8 ft height, 6 ft width) for an exempt maintenance activity -- vegetation trimming near trails -- unrelated to constructing our building.

reader_about: development standards, including a maximum front yard setback, within the Flex Space Overlay Zone, whose listed uses are industrial services, manufacturing, trade schools, and their accessory uses
reader_note: Table 19.404.4 lists only industrial/flex-space use categories with no residential category, so L2943's maximum front yard setback governs flex-space development, not a residential-only fourplex.

reader_about: minimum lot size for single detached dwellings created after June 3, 2022
reader_note: L29 states the standard applies to "Single detached dwellings" specifically -- not an attached four-unit building.

reader_about: height limit for sustainability-related accessory structures, specifically a small wind energy system's pole and turbine
reader_note: L495 governs "The pole and turbine" of a wind energy system, an accessory structure, not the primary residential building.

reader_about: minimum accessway/frontage width required for flag lots and back lots
reader_note: L657 applies specifically to "Flag lots," a lot configuration nothing on the card establishes for our building's lot.

reader_standard: distance triggering the one-to-four-unit building design standards (facade within 50 ft of a front/street-side lot line)
reader_about: applicability of the one-to-four-unit residential building and site design standards to plex developments
reader_note: L1007 states the building design standards apply when "the closest wall of the street-facing facade is within 50 ft of a front or street side lot line," and separately that "the site design standards apply to plex developments (i.e., 2 to 4 units)" outright -- our 4-unit building is exactly that plex development, so the site design standards bind unconditionally even though the specific numeric requirements are in the lines that follow and aren't shown on this card.

reader_about: size, illumination, and height limits for a sign permitted with an approved home occupation
reader_note: L2800 applies "on any property with an approved home occupation" -- our building's description includes no home occupation, so this signage standard is conditional on an elective use, not something the fourplex itself must satisfy.

reader_about: affordable-housing incentive allowing extra lot coverage above the base maximum
reader_note: L4633 is one line of an incentive/bonus program ("up to 10 percentage points increase over the base maximum") a developer may opt into -- nothing is required.

reader_about: minimum dimensions for off-street parking spaces and drive aisles, by parking angle, and required drive-aisle widths
reader_note: L489: "the minimum allowed width for a one-way drive aisle shall be 8 ft and the minimum allowed width for a two-way drive aisle shall be 16 ft." Our building has off-street parking, so its drive aisle(s) and stall dimensions (Table 19.606.1 above) would need to meet these minimums.

reader_about: definition of how tree diameter at breast height (DBH) is measured
reader_note: L3542 is a measurement-methodology definition (height 4.5 ft above ground, mid-point on sloped ground) for tree DBH, not a standard our building must meet.

reader_about: minimum lot size reduction to 5,000 square feet for 'flexible lots' in the RL zone, conditioned on subdivision density
reader_note: "(a) RL Zone. The minimum lot size may be reduced to 5,000 square feet if: (i) The density of the proposed subdivision does not exceed the density allowed in the zone" — this governs how a new lot may be created in a land division, not a standard our building must meet once sited on an existing lot.

reader_about: exemption from Historic Design Review for small accessory structures (under 120 sq ft, under 10 ft tall) in a side or rear yard
reader_note: "Construction of accessory structures under 120 square feet and 10 feet in height... in a side or rear yard" governs accessory structures like sheds and gazebos, not the main dwelling building.

reader_about: maximum height (50 feet) for places of worship or government buildings, conditioned on floor area
reader_note: The section heading is "PLACES OF WORSHIP OR GOVERNMENT BUILDINGS" and the line reads "The height of a place of worship or governmental building may be built to a maximum height of 50 feet" — a different building type entirely.

reader_about: minimum street frontage (75 feet) for a lot, with a reduction allowed on a finding about future subdivision density
reader_note: "C. Minimum Street Frontage: 75 feet. A reduced street frontage may be approved, based on a finding that the proposed lot frontage will not hinder the future development of the site to densities proposed in the Comprehensive Plan" — a lot-creation/subdivision dimensional standard, not something the building itself satisfies once the lot already exists.

reader_about: maximum height (30 feet) for exempt freestanding or wall-mounted flags
reader_note: "no exempt flag may be more than 30 feet in height" is a sign/flag regulation, unrelated to a residential building.

reader_about: size and spacing standards for additional ground-mounted subdivision entrance signs in residential zones
reader_note: "Additional ground mounted signs of 18 square feet or less shall be permitted for additional entrances... located at least 200 feet apart" governs signage, not the building.

reader_about: maximum height (20 feet) of freestanding or ground-mounted signs in the PDC, TC, PDI, and PF zones
reader_note: "The allowed height above ground of a freestanding or ground mounted sign is 20 feet" is a sign standard in non-residential zones, not applicable to our building.

reader_about: minimum land area (5 acres) and setbacks (50 feet) for a conditional-use public utility structure
reader_note: The heading below reads "(.06) Conditional Use Regulations—Public Utility Structures" and the line states "Front, Rear and Side Yard Setbacks: A minimum of 50 feet" for that use — a different, non-residential use type.

reader_about: paint/visibility standard for wireless communication towers over 200 feet tall
reader_note: "Towers more than 200 feet in height shall be painted in accordance with the Oregon State Aeronautics Division and Federal Aviation Administration rules" concerns communication towers, not our building.

reader_about: maximum height (50 feet) for wireless communication facilities located in the public right-of-way
reader_note: "the maximum height allowed in the right-of-way is 50 feet" governs wireless support facilities (WCF) in the ROW, an unrelated use.

reader_about: maximum height (20 feet) of trees/shrubs planted near guy wires of wireless support structures
reader_note: "Trees and shrubs in the vicinity of guy wires shall be of a kind that would not exceed 20 feet in height" is landscaping tied to a wireless facility's guy wires, not our building.

reader_standard: minimum building setback from property lines
reader_about: a general building setback formula tied to building height, under a table headed 'Development Standards'
reader_note: "buildings must be set back from all property lines a minimum of 1 foot for each foot of building height" is stated as a general 'buildings' standard with no stated exclusion for a residential building, so a ~26-foot-tall structure would need roughly a 26-foot setback.

reader_about: exemption allowing small water cisterns (6 feet or less) inside required side/rear setbacks
reader_note: "Water collection cisterns that are 6 feet or less in height are allowed in required side and rear setbacks" is an accessory-structure allowance, not a standard for the main dwelling.

reader_about: retaining wall height (4 feet max) and setback (3 feet) standards, appearing beneath a table captioned 'Institutional Development Standards'
reader_note: "Retaining walls are limited to 4 feet in height measured from the bottom of the footing... must be set back at least 3 feet from other street-facing retaining" — like a fence, a retaining wall is an incidental site feature built only if grading requires one, not a standard the building itself must meet, and the table just above it is scoped to institutional development.

reader_about: exemption allowing small water cisterns (6 feet or less) inside side/rear setbacks, including setbacks abutting a residential zone
reader_note: "Water cisterns that are 6 feet or less in height are allowed in side and rear setbacks" is an accessory-structure allowance, not a standard for the dwelling itself.

reader_about: fire-safety vegetation height limit (under 2 feet) for silviculture/forest practices on sloped land
reader_note: The section heading is "FOREST PRACTICES" and the line "All other vegetation should be kept less than 2 feet in height" concerns wildfire fuel management on forestland, wholly unrelated to residential construction.

reader_about: purpose statement for the LR-10 (Urban Low Density Residential) base zone, describing its 10,000 sq ft minimum lot size for one dwelling
reader_note: The heading is "39.4868 PURPOSE" and the text "This base zone is defined as an Urban Low Density Residential Base zone with a minimum lot size of 10,000 square feet for one dwelling" is descriptive intent framed around a single dwelling, not the chapter's operative lot-size/density standard.

reader_standard: minimum no-build buffer from Fairview Creek
reader_about: a mapped creek-corridor conservation easement along Fairview Creek and Clear Creek within Fairview Village, plus tree-removal mitigation planting ratios
reader_note: "Within the 100-foot protected area along Fairview Creek, development and resource alteration, other than mitigation or enhancement, will be prohibited within 70 feet of the corridor centered on the creek" — a mapped riparian buffer that any lot containing the creek, including ours, would have to keep clear of.

reader_about: definition of how 'building height' is measured, including the reference elevation point on sloped sites
reader_note: "An elevation 10 feet higher than the lowest grade when the sidewalk or ground surface... is more than 10 feet above the lowest grade" is a method for measuring height (a definition), not itself a height limit.

reader_about: development standards for the VO zone: a height cap and a statement that there are no setback requirements
reader_note: "Buildings within this zone may not exceed 55 feet in height" is a general height limit stated for 'Buildings within this zone' with no exclusion of residential use; our ~26-foot building would have to satisfy it, though comfortably. L61's 'no setback requirements' means setbacks do not additionally bind here.

reader_about: construction and illumination standards for public pedestrian ways and trails (width, lighting height, foot-candle level)
reader_note: "Pedestrian ways shall be illuminated... with pedestrian scale lighting not to exceed 20 feet in height" is a public-improvement/streetscape standard for shared circulation infrastructure, not a standard for the building itself.

reader_standard: minimum window coverage of ground-level walls facing a sidewalk or public space
reader_about: a 'blank wall' glazing design standard for ground-level exterior walls that abut sidewalks, plazas, or public open space
reader_note: "Windows must occupy at least 50 percent of the length and 25 percent of the ground level wall area... applies to the ground level of exterior building walls which abut sidewalks, plazas, or other public open spaces" — a design standard our building's street-facing ground floor would have to meet; the 25 percent wall-area figure is a second, related number.

reader_about: design standards for cottage-cluster garages and accessory structures (maximum size and garage door width)
reader_note: The section heading is "Design standards for cottage clusters" — an explicitly excluded building type, not our four-unit attached townhome.

reader_about: common open space requirement for multiple-unit developments in the Residential Medium Density (RM) district
reader_note: "a minimum of 10 percent of the site area shall be designated and permanently reserved as usable common open space in all multiple-unit developments" — a four-unit attached townhome squarely qualifies as a multiple-unit development.

reader_about: optional height bonus (up to 20 ft) and off-street parking credit options for developments in the Town Center Commercial District
reader_note: L273 says a height bonus 'is allowed' if a developer chooses to meet criteria in Table 19.65.070 -- nothing is required. L275's parking credit is likewise elective, not a standard the building must meet.

reader_about: lot coverage and floor area ratio for the Corridor Commercial District
reader_note: L98 states plainly: 'There are no maximum lot coverage or floor area ratio requirements' in this district, so nothing is imposed by this section.

reader_about: an optional conditional-use height bonus to 55 feet in the Corridor Commercial District
reader_note: The marked line (L128) is the 'C. Performance Option' -- an elective increase to 55 feet obtainable only through a conditional use permit. Nothing here is mandatory.

reader_about: maximum lot coverage (85 percent) in the Light Industrial District
reader_note: L102 sets an 85 percent lot coverage cap, but the use table above (L45-66) lists only industrial and CU-only commercial uses; a residential fourplex is not a use this district's standards reach.

reader_about: an optional conditional-use height bonus to 55 feet in the Light Industrial District
reader_note: Marked L110 is the 'B. Performance Option,' an elective CUP-based increase; also the Light Industrial District use table does not list a residential fourplex.

reader_about: maximum lot coverage (85 percent) in the General Industrial District
reader_note: L137 sets an 85 percent lot coverage cap, but the district table above (L37-58) lists only industrial uses; a residential fourplex isn't among them.

reader_about: an optional conditional-use height bonus to 55 feet in the General Industrial District
reader_note: Marked L157 is the 'B. Performance Option' -- an elective CUP-based increase, and the district's use table is industrial, not residential.

reader_about: definition of what floor area is excluded when measuring 'building height' (basements, low attics, roof area, roof equipment)
reader_note: This is the definitions chapter describing what does NOT count toward the height measurement, not a standalone numeric standard the building must meet -- a definition, per the instructions, is a 'no.'

reader_about: minimum net density (6.22 units/acre) for the Low Density Residential -5 (LDR-5) district
reader_note: L59's minimum-density figure applies only 'for all subdivisions, and for those partitions of parent parcels greater than 20,000 square feet' -- placing one fourplex on its own existing lot is neither a subdivision nor a qualifying partition.

reader_about: minimum net density (4.35 units/acre) for the Low Density Residential -7 (LDR-7) district
reader_note: Same structure as LDR-5: L67's minimum only applies 'for all subdivisions, and for those partitions of parent parcels greater than 20,000 square feet' -- not our single-lot building.

reader_about: permitted housing types and maximum net density for the Transit Low-Density Residential (TLDR) district
reader_note: L73-75 lists 'quadplexes, townhouses' among the permitted types and states 'a maximum net density for single detached units of 20 units per acre and for townhouses of 25 units per acre' -- our four-unit attached townhome is the townhouse category, capped at 25 units/acre, which a small lot could exceed.

reader_about: residential net density standards for the Transition Residential (TR) district
reader_note: L89-90: 'The residential net density for single detached units is 6.22 to 14.52 or 18.15 units per acre, depending on site size, and 25 units per acre for townhouses' -- our attached four-unit building is the townhouse category and must not exceed 25 units/acre.

reader_about: maximum building height (base 40 ft/3 stories, optional bonus to 65 ft with fire protection) and on-site business-activity restrictions in the Commercial district
reader_note: This is 'Additional Commercial Land Use District Standards'; the marked line (L194) is itself the optional fire-protection height bonus, and the section governs a commercial district, not a residential fourplex use.

reader_about: maximum height of roof-mounted wind energy systems in commercial districts
reader_note: This governs an optional accessory wind turbine a developer might add to a commercial building; our fourplex has no wind energy system, and this is a commercial-district provision.

reader_about: maximum height of ground-mounted solar energy systems in industrial districts
reader_note: Accessory solar-equipment height limit for the Heavy/General Industrial districts -- our building includes no solar energy system and isn't an industrial use.

reader_about: maximum height of ground-mounted wind energy systems in industrial districts
reader_note: An optional accessory wind-turbine standard for industrial districts, not applicable to our residential building.

reader_about: maximum height of roof-mounted and ground-mounted wind energy systems in Corridor design/plan districts
reader_note: L684-688 caps an optional accessory wind turbine's height; our fourplex has no wind energy system, so nothing here binds it.

reader_about: an optional sidewalk canopy 'bonus element' plus downtown height/setback bonus notes for the Downtown district
reader_note: The section heading itself is 'BONUS ELEMENTS,' and the marked line (L610) is titled 'Canopy Over Sidewalks Where Not Otherwise Required' -- an elective feature a developer may add, not a mandatory standard.

reader_about: maximum height of roof-mounted wind energy systems in Downtown districts
reader_note: An accessory wind-turbine height cap for Downtown districts; our building has no such system.

reader_about: maximum height of ground-mounted solar energy systems in the Civic Neighborhood Plan District
reader_note: L448 caps an optional accessory solar installation at 20 feet; our building includes no solar energy system.

reader_about: maximum height of roof-mounted solar energy system frames in the Civic Neighborhood Plan District
reader_note: L441 caps an optional roof-mounted solar frame at 10 feet above the roof; not applicable since our building has no solar system.

reader_about: maximum height of roof-mounted wind energy systems in the Civic Neighborhood Plan District
reader_note: L458 caps an optional roof-mounted wind turbine at 10 feet above the roof height; our building has no wind energy system.

reader_about: housing types and maximum net density for the Very Low-Density Residential - Springwater (VLDR-SW) district
reader_note: L116-118: the district is 'intended for Single Detached Dwellings and Middle Housing... at a maximum net density for Single Detached Dwellings of 3.6 units per acre, and for Townhouses of 14.4 units per acre.' A four-unit attached townhome is Middle Housing/townhouse type and must not exceed 14.4 units/acre.

reader_about: residential net density for the Low-Density Residential - Springwater (LDR-SW) district
reader_note: L121-123: the district runs 'at an average net density for single detached units of 5.8 to 7.3 dwelling units per acre and 5.8 to 25 units per acre for Townhouses' -- our attached four-unit building falls in the townhouse range, and a compact lot could push past the 25/acre upper bound.

reader_about: categories used to measure design and building-form variety across multiple structures within a larger middle-housing development area
reader_note: The marked line ('Building lot coverage. Lot coverage does not exceed 50 percent') is one of several 'design feature categories' used only to apply a variety requirement across a multi-structure 'development area' (L829-832); a single four-unit building on its own lot has nothing to vary against.

reader_about: height limits applied near lower-density zoned lots, tiered by distance from the lot line
reader_note: "On the portion of the site less than or equal to 35 feet from the lot line of a lot zoned LDR-5, LDR7, TR or TLDR, the maximum building height shall be 30 feet" (L49) is a citywide height-transition standard our building would have to meet if sited near one of those zones.

reader_about: sill height limits for windows/openings in freestanding parking structures
reader_note: The 6-foot maximum sill height (L1090) governs a dedicated 'Parking Structure' (a multi-level garage building), not surface parking or an attached garage serving a residential fourplex.

reader_standard: maximum height of obstructions within the clear vision area
reader_about: driveway approach placement and the clear-vision sight triangle at driveways and intersections
reader_note: "No fence, wall, landscaping, sign, structure, or parked vehicle that would impede visibility between a height of 3 feet and 10 feet" may sit in the Clear Vision Area (L71); any lot with a driveway to a public street, including ours, must keep that triangle clear. The unmarked table above also sets driveway approach widths (9 ft minimum, 24 ft maximum for residential).

reader_about: building setbacks under an industrial/employment zone chapter's development standards
reader_note: The 1-foot-of-setback-per-foot-of-height rule (L186) is Chapter 33.100's development standard, an industrial/employment zoning chapter a residential-only fourplex would not be built in.

reader_about: an exception letting small water cisterns sit inside a required setback for detached accessory structures
reader_note: "Water collection cisterns that are 6 feet or less in height are allowed in required side and rear setbacks" (L985) is a permissive exception for an optional accessory item, not a standard the building itself must meet.

reader_about: height and setback limits for retaining walls, an optional site feature
reader_note: "Retaining walls are limited to 4 feet in height... must be set back at least 3 feet" (L2105) only applies if a retaining wall is built; nothing on the page shows this vacant/cleared lot needs one.

reader_about: density and use description of the RMP (manufactured dwelling park) zone
reader_note: "The RMP zone... allows manufactured dwelling parks. Allowed density may be up to 29 units per acre" (L138-139) describes a different use (manufactured home parks assembled off-site), not an attached four-unit townhome.

reader_about: permitted rooftop projections that may exceed the height limit
reader_note: "Chimneys, vents, flag poles... with a width, depth, or diameter of 5 feet or less may extend above the height limit" (L932) is an optional exception a developer may take, not something that must be satisfied.

reader_about: site area, FAR, height, setback and coverage standards specific to institutional development
reader_note: The table and its section heading ('33.120.275 Development Standards for Institutions') apply only to institutional uses like schools or churches, not a residential fourplex.

reader_about: adjusted building coverage and landscaping percentages for lots that front a shared court or common green
reader_note: "The building coverage on lots with a front lot line on a shared court or common green is 5 percent greater than the building coverage of the base zone" (L2193) applies only to that specific frontage type; our building fronts a public street with a driveway, not a shared court or common green.

reader_about: cistern setback exception amid an institutional development standards table
reader_note: L2005 repeats the same cistern-in-setback exception seen elsewhere ('Water collection cisterns... are allowed in side and rear setbacks'), an optional accessory item, inside a table (120-8) governing institutional development.

reader_about: cistern setback exception for detached accessory structures
reader_note: "Water cisterns that are 6 feet or less in height are allowed in side and rear setbacks" (L1392) is an optional accessory-structure allowance, not a building requirement.

reader_about: screening/setback requirements for rooftop mechanical equipment facing a residential zone, in an employment-zone chapter
reader_note: The 3-feet-of-setback-per-foot-of-height-or-screen rule (L831) governs equipment on buildings in Chapter 33.150's employment-zone standards near an R zone; a residential-only fourplex would not typically be developed in that zone, and the rule binds only if rooftop equipment sits near the zone's edge.

reader_about: cistern setback exception for detached accessory structures
reader_note: "Water cisterns that are 6 feet or less in height are allowed in side and rear setbacks" (L955) is the same optional accessory allowance seen in other zones, not a building requirement.

reader_about: the measurement method for determining a tree's trunk diameter
reader_note: "the trunk is measured at right angles to the trunk 4-1/2 feet along the center of the trunk axis" (L438) is a measurement procedure for tree preservation purposes, not a standard applied to the building.

reader_about: definition of an airport imaginary surface (height zone) in the code's definitions chapter
reader_note: This sits in the jurisdiction's definitions document (1.020.definitions.txt) and describes a technical airspace surface ('upward extending to a height of three hundred fifty (350) feet above the airport elevation', L922) used to define a term, not an operative building standard.

reader_about: definition of 'Below-Grade Crawl Space' for flood/height-measurement purposes
reader_note: "Below-Grade Crawl Space. Means..." (L1130-1133) is a defined term in the code's definitions chapter, not a standard the building must satisfy.

reader_about: lot width and coverage standards for Industrial Park, Light Industrial, and General Industrial zoning districts
reader_note: The table heading '3.430 Dimensional Standards for Industrial Zoning Districts' with columns 'IP LI GI' (L1112-1114) applies to industrial zones, not a residential building.

reader_about: height/setback compliance for optional play structures within a development's recreation area
reader_note: "Any play structure exceeding ten (10) feet in height must comply with the underlying zoning district setbacks" (L1196) is conditional on choosing to install a tall play structure as part of an optional recreation amenity.

reader_about: roof pitch requirement specific to manufactured home dwellings
reader_note: "The manufactured home shall have a pitched roof. The minimum slope shall be not less than a nominal three (3) feet in height for each twelve (12) feet in width" (L1421-1422) governs HUD-code manufactured homes, a different factory-chassis dwelling type from a modular quadplex.

reader_about: maximum height for optional sight-obscuring hedges/landscaping along a specific commercial corridor
reader_note: "Sight-obscuring hedges or landscaping shall not exceed a height of forty-two (42) inches" (L1602-1603) only constrains landscaping if a developer chooses to plant a sight-obscuring hedge; nothing on the page shows landscaping of that kind is mandatory.

reader_about: minimum size and clearance for commercial/industrial loading areas
reader_note: "The required loading area shall not be less than ten (10) feet in width by twenty-five (25) feet in length and shall have an unobstructed height of fourteen (14) feet" (L617-618) is a loading-dock standard for commercial/industrial-scale uses, not a small residential fourplex.

reader_about: an elective menu of design bonus options (plaza, outdoor recreation, extra ground-floor height) for the Neighborhood Commercial zone
reader_note: "Table 230-6. Menu of Options for Additional Requirements" (L198) lists point-earning options a developer may choose; even option P3's ground-floor height for residential use (L213) is one alternative among several, and the zone itself (NC) is commercial, not necessarily our building's district.
